I&D the abscess; defer definitive excision until quiescent; off-midline closure (Karydakis, Bascom, rhomboid flap) — lower recurrence than midline closure; hygiene and hair removal after healing.
ventral mesh rectopexy — lowest recurrence (< 10%), preserves continence and sexual function
Altemeier (perineal rectosigmoidectomy) or Delorme (mucosal sleeve) — no pelvic dissection, quicker recovery, higher recurrence (~20%). Overall recurrence ~15%

conservative (bulking, loperamide, bowel regimen) → biofeedback → overlapping sphincteroplasty (obstetric/traumatic defect — ~85% initial cure) → sacral nerve stimulation (refractory, intact/repaired sphincter). Treat the cause (prolapse, IBD).
60-year-old with bleeding, weight loss and a palpable inguinal node → anal (or rectal) cancer before haemorrhoids.
EUA + biopsy · MRI pelvis · CT chest/abdomen/pelvis · inguinal nodes ± biopsy · offer HIV testing.
